title: Deterministic Verification and a Single‑Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: a Paired, Shared‑Candidate Study
abstract: We report a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the same LLM-generated configuration candidate. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation call per intent reused for both episodes) we generated one candidate per natural-language intent with gpt-5-mini for N = 250 pairs and evaluated two episodes per intent: baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (deterministic_netops_validator_v5; if failing, permit one automated repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251. Results: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100.0%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The single discordant pair was converted to pass by the single permitted repair. Important scope note (explicit and preregistered): the preregistered sim‑to‑real (production-like) confirmatory contrast was not executed; the confirmatory estimand reported here applies to the synthetic/emulation partition only. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the study evidence bundle referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly investigated as intent-to-configuration translators for network operations (NetOps). They can draft device CLI sequences from operator intents, but stochastic generation risks syntax errors, incorrect command ordering, and vendor-specific semantic subtleties that can produce unsafe or non-functional changes. Community work documents both LLM feasibility for producing usable drafts and the continuing need for deterministic verification or human oversight [1],[2].

A common architectural response is generate–verify–repair (GVR): generate a candidate, run a deterministic validator, and, if defects are detected, attempt bounded automated repair before acceptance [3],[4]. GVR pipelines reliably eliminate many mechanically checkable errors (syntax, local policy violations) but the marginal benefit of adding deterministic validation and a bounded repair stage may be small when modern LLM outputs already conform to validator encodings in constrained tasks. Prior work has not, to our knowledge, measured that marginal verifier+single-repair effect under a paired design that reuses the identical model candidate across conditions.

This paper reports a preregistered paired experiment that isolates the validator/repair marginal effect under shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation per intent reused across baseline and guarded episodes). We executed N_pairs = 250 constrained intents with gpt-5-mini on a synthetic/emulation partition and used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 for full_intent_constraint_validation. All run artifacts and the preregistration are archived. Our contribution is an artifact-backed, numerically exact quantification of the marginal validator-detected improvement and an analysis of why that improvement was small in this constrained setting.
sections.related_work:
Surveys and empirical NetOps studies establish that (a) LLMs can produce draft configurations in controlled setups [1],[2], (b) deterministic validators (model checking, header-space/Batfish-style analyses) provide mechanized property checks used in GVR pipelines [3],[5], and (c) generate-and-verify and program-repair workflows reduce mechanically verifiable error classes in code and configuration domains though deeper semantic correctness and cross-vendor subtleties remain challenging [4],[6]. Security analyses of prompt-injection and retrieval threats highlight the need for filtering and verification layers but note that adaptive attackers are an unresolved threat [7].

This work differs by (i) employing a preregistered paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics that isolates only the validator/repair marginal effect on identical generated candidates, (ii) providing complete provider-call accounting and deterministic reconciliation for stage-level mapping of generation and repair calls, and (iii) archiving validator traces and reconciliation artifacts so reported numeric outcomes are auditable.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand: The experiment was preregistered as study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (preregistration SHA-256 = 7a984dbf7265c9a7...). The confirmatory estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline in a paired-binary design with N_pairs = 250. The preregistration froze shared_initial_candidate semantics, allowed at most one automated repair per episode, exclusion rules, the exact analysis tests (exact McNemar two-sided and paired-bootstrap percentile CIs), and the model-call budget.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and provider accounting (explicit). By preregistered design exactly one initial model-generation call was produced per intent; that identical generated candidate was reused for both episodes (baseline and guarded). The execution's provider accounting reconciles to model_calls_used = 251, which decomposes as 250 shared initial-generation calls plus 1 repair call. Adapter audit fields label these events with nonstandard adapter counters (condition_counts {"shared": 250, "guarded": 1}) because the adapter reports the 250 shared initial-generation events under the adapter "shared" label and the single repair-stage generation under the "guarded" label; stage_counts record {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1}. This paragraph explicitly states the mapping so readers cannot infer independent first-pass generations per condition.

Tasks and constraints: A deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) produced 250 constrained intents. Each task payload encoded initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and difficulty labels (medium/hard/very_hard). Tasks exercised workflow constraints (e.g., make-before-break uplink switchover, paired-link atomic MTU changes) and protected interfaces that must not be modified. Tasks and full manifest are archived.

Model, validator, and repair semantics: Declared model for initial generations was gpt-5-mini. The guarded pipeline submitted the shared candidate to deterministic_netops_validator_v5, which implements full_intent_constraint_validation (parsing CLI, checking required_sequence ordering, workflow constraints, and comparing a final_state snapshot to the task's expected_final_state). If the validator returned valid=false for a guarded episode, the pipeline permitted a single deterministic, template-driven repair (syntactic/order fixes) and re-submitted the repaired candidate once. No iterative or human-in-loop repair was permitted by design.

Inclusion and contamination rules: The preregistered exclusion rules removed items failing deterministic vendor parsers that prevented verification or containing denylisted tokens; contamination detectors flagged instruction-like embedded tokens. Flagged or excluded items would be documented and treated by preregistered sensitivity analyses. For this confirmatory run no episodes were excluded or flagged.
sections.results:
Execution summary and reconciliation. Execution completed the preregistered confirmatory partition with planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, complete_pair_count = 250, and model_calls_used = 251. Provider-call accounting maps to 250 shared initial-generation calls and 1 repair call (stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 250; repair = 1).

Primary binary outcomes and contingency. Validator-scored successes: baseline_success_count = 249 (baseline_success_rate = 0.996), guarded_success_count = 250 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). The paired contingency observed is n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The single discordant pair corresponds to the only exercised repair and was converted from baseline-fail to guarded-pass; repair-conversion rate = 1/250 = 0.004 (0.4%).

Statistical inference. Exact McNemar two-sided test on discordant counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0) returns p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for guarded − baseline (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) is [0.0, 0.012] (i.e., 0 – 1.2 percentage points). These numeric outputs are preserved in the archived analysis artifacts.

Representative validator diagnostics and repair trace. Passed episodes show parsed_command_count and required_command_count equal to the task payload required_sequence length; representative task-000003 (hard) reports parsed_command_count = 6 and required_command_count = 6 and valid = true for both episodes. Only one automated repair was invoked; its repair trace and the corresponding guarded scoring artifact are archived for audit.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation of a near‑null marginal effect. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and the constrained synthetic/emulation task bank, the marginal verifier-detected benefit of a deterministic validator plus a single repair was small: initial gpt-5-mini candidates satisfied the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases and the single permitted repair converted the lone failing candidate. The paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (1.2 pp) empirically bounds the maximum possible verifier-detected improvement under these study conditions.

Why the gain was small (artifact-grounded factors). Three artifact-grounded factors explain the small guarded gain: (1) the deterministic task generator encoded constrained intents and allowed_touched_fields that reduced ambiguity and favored well-formed CLI sequences; (2) gpt-5-mini produced highly consistent, syntactically well-formed sequences for these constrained intents; and (3) the deterministic validator checks mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, final_state snapshot) and does not capture broader behavioral correctness in live protocol execution or emergent cross-device interactions.

Power, assumptions, and limitations. The preregistered power calculation assumed a baseline pass rate ≈ 0.90 when selecting N_pairs = 250 to detect a 15 pp effect with ≈80% power. The observed baseline pass rate (0.996) is substantially higher than assumed; this reduces power to detect small absolute improvements and makes the bootstrap CI the most informative quantity. Construct validity is limited because the validator measures mechanistic compliance, not live protocol-level correctness. External validity is limited to the synthetic/emulation partition: the preregistered sim-to-real production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed and remains future work. Security evaluations against adaptive prompt-injection were not performed here.

Operational implications (bounded). In tightly constrained emulation tasks with a capable LLM the marginal verifier-detected improvement from a single repair may be small. This does not imply validators are unnecessary in broader or adversarial deployments: validator scope, multi-iteration repair, human escalation, production heterogeneity, and adversaries can materially change the benefit of GVR pipelines.

Reproducibility and auditability. All run artifacts (raw responses, execution manifest, validator traces, repair traces, deterministic reconciliation, and analysis outputs) are archived in the study evidence bundle referenced in the Disclosure Statement. Key numeric reconciliation facts reported above (model_calls_used = 251; stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 250, repair: 1}; contingency n11=249,n10=1,n01=0,n00=0; bootstrap parameters) are reproducible from the archived manifests and analysis CSVs.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed, preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure the verifier-detected marginal benefit of deterministic validation plus one permitted automated repair on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates. On N = 250 constrained synthetic intents generated with gpt-5-mini, initial candidates passed the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases; the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate via the sole permitted repair. Observed paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp]; p = 1.0). We explicitly disclose that the preregistered sim‑to‑real confirmatory contrast was not executed and that the reported confirmatory estimand applies only to the synthetic/emulation partition. Broader production, adversarial, multi-model, and multi-iteration repair evaluations remain necessary to assess generality. Execution and analysis artifacts supporting these exact numeric claims are archived and referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

disclosure_statement:
Human role and autonomy boundary: After the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher autonomy lock, the autonomous system performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted repair execution, analysis, drafting, peer-review, revision, and finalization without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the topic family and performed pre-lock infrastructure development only; no human manually edited manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.

Models, tools, and framework: declared model = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses); deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The guarded generate–verify–repair flow permitted at most one automated repair per episode as specified in the preregistration. Execution manifest recorded planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, and model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial_generation + 1 repair) as reconciled by the adapter audit.

Preregistration and immutable prompt reference: preregistration study id = study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (preregistration SHA-256 = 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede). Immutable master prompt initiating the autonomous run: provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Full execution and analysis artifacts (raw responses, validator and repair traces, deterministic reconciliation, provider-call audit, and analysis CSVs) are archived in the study evidence bundle; the bundle's full manifest is archived at execution/execution_manifest.json in the evidence bundle. The paper reports only analyses that are supported by those archived artifacts.

Executed confirmatory estimand and deviation disclosure: The preregistration included synthetic/emulation, community, and production-like partitions and a preregistered sim-to-real confirmatory contrast. Deviation disclosure (explicit): the preregistered sim-to-real production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed in this run; the executed confirmatory estimand reported here (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) was evaluated on the synthetic/emulation partition only (N_pairs = 250; shared_initial_candidate semantics).
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed.
Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, expected final_state) but did not measure live protocol-level behavioral correctness.
Single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adversarial and retrieval-based attacks (adaptive prompt-injection, vendor-targeted exploit vectors) and large-scale production heterogeneity were not exercised and remain open threats.
